source.title: Action chunking as conditional policy compression

confidence_rationale: Strong venue and an unusually clean theory-plus-confirmation structure (a normative model whose behavioural predictions -- reaction time reduction, chunking increasing with working-memory load, chunking freeing capacity -- were experimentally confirmed). Held below 0.8 because it is a 2025 paper without independent replication, and because the resource currency it optimises (working-memory capacity) is not obviously REE's currency (combinatorial rollout cost).
failure_signatures: A pure policy-compression account predicts chunks persist for as long as the environment's temporal structure remains compressible; it supplies no pressure that would re-decompose a chunk on prediction failure, so it is silent-to-tensioned on ARC-070's direction.
If REE's rollout cost is combinatorial-planning cost rather than a storage/capacity constraint, the model's central trade-off does not transfer and its predicted chunking triggers would not apply.

mapping.source_claim_statement: Action chunking arises from optimising a trade-off between reward and conditional policy complexity. Chunking compresses a policy when the environment has temporal structure that can be leveraged for action selection, reducing the memory needed to encode the policy; empirically, chunking reduces conditional policy complexity and reaction times, increases with working-memory load, and lowers overall working-memory load.
mapping.ree_translation: Gives ARC-069 a normative account of WHY the grain should rescale at all, and specifically a candidate trigger for the composition leg (ARC-071): compress when exploitable temporal structure exists and the resource constraint binds. This is a substantive refinement of -- arguably a correction to -- ARC-071's currently-proposed trigger of raw repetition count plus outcome consistency, since repetition is only a proxy for the compressibility the model says is actually doing the work.
mapping.mapping_caveat: The binding constraint in Lai et al. is a capacity limit on policy storage (working memory). ARC-069's motivation is the combinatorial cost of rollout at fine grain -- a search-cost, not a storage-cost. These may coincide in practice but they are not the same quantity, and a Phase-0-style REE implementation that chunks on a storage criterion could compress exactly the sequences that rollout does not benefit from. The paper also addresses composition only; it has nothing to say about decomposition.
mapping.source_context: Human behavioural experiments (sequence learning with reaction-time and working-memory-load manipulations) paired with a rate-distortion / policy-compression model.

confidence_components.notes: Transfer risk is comparatively low -- this is a computational account of an artificial-agent-shaped problem -- but the cost-currency mismatch noted in the caveat is the live hazard, and it sits in mapping_fidelity rather than transfer_risk.
